RENAMED the module the PRD and design doc both call `scripts/queue.py` to `scripts/docket.py` (and `test_queue.py` to `test_docket.py`). Reason: `queue` is a Python STDLIB module name. `skills/brief-portfolio/scripts/collect.py` imports `concurrent.futures`, which loads stdlib `queue` into sys.modules; after that any `import queue` returns the stdlib module, so 33 of 941 tests failed in the first full-suite run since this PRD started. Reproduced minimally: `uv run --with pytest pytest skills/brief-portfolio skills/distil-memory/scripts/test_queue.py` = 32 failed, while the same file alone passes. Per-task verification never caught it because it runs the new tests in isolation, where nothing has imported stdlib queue yet. Rejected the two alternatives: force-loading the local module into sys.modules[queue] from a conftest would hand brief-portfolio the WRONG queue module for the rest of the session, and an importlib-by-path shim in each test file leaves the collision live for any real driver script that does `import queue`. The filename is the defect, so the filename is what changed. `docket` follows the sibling naming register (corpus, funnel, distil, dedup, proposal, write) and collides with nothing. The on-disk data file stays `distil-memory-queue.json` - no collision there, and renaming it would orphan an existing queue.
